title: Linear Equations & Systems
sub: 20 FRQs + 25 MCQs • Difficulty Progression • Cross-Lesson Synthesis

sections.heading: Part I — Free-Response Questions (FRQs): Foundational Fluency (1–7)

questions.q: Solve each linear equation for $x$ and verify your solution by substitution:
questions.answer: Combine like terms on each side, isolate the variable term, and divide by the coefficient of $x$.

questions.q: A line passes through the points $A(-3, 7)$ and $B(5, -9)$ in the $xy$-plane. Determine (a) the slope of the line, (b) its equation in slope-intercept form $y = mx + b$, and (c) its $x$-intercept.
questions.answer: (a) Slope $m = \dfrac{-9 - 7}{5 - (-3)} = \dfrac{-16}{8} = -2$. (b) Using $(5, -9)$: $-9 = -2(5) + b \Rightarrow b = 1$, so $y = -2x + 1$. (c) Setting $y = 0$ gives $-2x + 1 = 0 \Rightarrow x = \dfrac{1}{2}$, so the $x$-intercept is $\left(\dfrac{1}{2}, 0\right)$.

questions.q: Convert the standard-form linear equation $6x - 8y = 24$ into slope-intercept form, state the slope and both intercepts, and compute the area of the right triangle bounded by the line and the coordinate axes.
questions.answer: Solving for $y$: $-8y = -6x + 24 \Rightarrow y = \dfrac{3}{4}x - 3$. The slope is $m = \dfrac{3}{4}$, the $y$-intercept is $(0, -3)$, and the $x$-intercept is $(4, 0)$. The right triangle with legs $4$ and $3$ has area $A = \dfrac{1}{2}(4)(3) = 6$ square units.

questions.q: A cloud-computing server plan charges a fixed monthly maintenance fee plus a constant rate per gigabyte of outbound data transfer. Using $120\,\mathrm{GB}$ costs $86$ dollars, and using $270\,\mathrm{GB}$ costs $131$ dollars. Write a linear function $C(g)$ for the monthly cost (in dollars) of $g\,\mathrm{GB}$, and interpret both the slope and $C(0)$ in context.
questions.answer: Rate per GB: $m = \dfrac{131 - 86}{270 - 120} = \dfrac{45}{150} = 0.30$ dollars per GB. Using $(120, 86)$: $86 = 0.30(120) + b \Rightarrow b = 50$. Thus $C(g) = 0.30g + 50$, where $0.30$ is the cost in dollars per additional gigabyte and $C(0) = 50$ dollars is the fixed monthly base fee.

questions.q: Determine the equation of the line passing through $(-4, 6)$ that is (a) parallel to $3x + 2y = 10$, and (b) perpendicular to $3x + 2y = 10$. Write both answers in slope-intercept form.
questions.answer: The given line has slope $m = -\dfrac{3}{2}$. (a) Parallel slope $m_{\parallel} = -\dfrac{3}{2}$: $y - 6 = -\dfrac{3}{2}(x + 4) \Rightarrow y = -\dfrac{3}{2}x$. (b) Perpendicular slope $m_{\perp} = \dfrac{2}{3}$: $y - 6 = \dfrac{2}{3}(x + 4) \Rightarrow y = \dfrac{2}{3}x + \dfrac{26}{3}$.

questions.q: Rearrange the literal thermal-expansion formula $L = L_0\left(1 + \alpha(T - T_0)\right)$ to express the temperature $T$ in terms of $L, L_0, \alpha,$ and $T_0$.
questions.answer: Divide by $L_0$: $\dfrac{L}{L_0} = 1 + \alpha(T - T_0) \Rightarrow \dfrac{L - L_0}{L_0} = \alpha(T - T_0) \Rightarrow T = T_0 + \dfrac{L - L_0}{\alpha L_0}$.

questions.target: Conditions for No Solution vs. Infinitely Many Solutions
questions.q: Find the value of the constant $k$ for which the linear equation $4(3x - k) + 6 = 2(6x + 9)$ has infinitely many real solutions.
questions.answer: Expand both sides: $12x - 4k + 6 = 12x + 18$. For infinitely many solutions (an identity), the constant terms must match: $-4k + 6 = 18 \Rightarrow -4k = 12 \Rightarrow k = -3$.

sections.heading: Part I — Free-Response Questions (FRQs): Intermediate Modeling (8–14)

questions.q: In the $xy$-plane shown, line $\ell_1$ has equation $y = \dfrac{1}{2}x + 3$ and line $\ell_2$ passes through $(0, -2)$ and $(4, -10)$ so that $\ell_1 \perp \ell_2$. Find the exact coordinates of their intersection point $P$.
questions.answer: Line $\ell_2$ has slope $m_2 = \dfrac{-10 - (-2)}{4 - 0} = -2$, so its equation is $y = -2x - 2$. Setting $\dfrac{1}{2}x + 3 = -2x - 2$ gives $\dfrac{5}{2}x = -5 \Rightarrow x = -2$, and $y = \dfrac{1}{2}(-2) + 3 = 2$. Thus $P = (-2, 2)$.

questions.q: An chemist mixes a $18\%$ saline solution with a $42\%$ saline solution to produce $600\,\mathrm{mL}$ of a $28\%$ saline solution. How many milliliters of each solution must be used?
questions.answer: Let $x$ be the volume (in mL) of the $18\%$ solution; then $600 - x$ is the volume of the $42\%$ solution. Set up the mass-balance equation: $0.18x + 0.42(600 - x) = 0.28(600) \Rightarrow -0.24x + 252 = 168 \Rightarrow 0.24x = 84 \Rightarrow x = 350\,\mathrm{mL}$ of the $18\%$ solution and $600 - 350 = 250\,\mathrm{mL}$ of the $42\%$ solution.

questions.q: Solve the absolute value equation $3|2x - 5| - 7 = 14$ and plot both solutions on a number line, stating the midpoint and distance from the midpoint to each solution.
questions.answer: Isolate the absolute value: $3|2x - 5| = 21 \Rightarrow |2x - 5| = 7$. Thus $2x - 5 = 7 \Rightarrow x = 6$, or $2x - 5 = -7 \Rightarrow x = -1$. The midpoint is $x = 2.5$ and each solution lies at distance $3.5$ from $2.5$.

questions.target: Parametric Linear Equations with No Solution
questions.q: For what value(s) of the parameter $a$ does the linear equation $(2a - 5)x + 3a = 7x + 12$ have no solution?
questions.answer: Rewrite as $(2a - 12)x = 12 - 3a$. A single-variable linear equation $Mx = N$ has no solution if and only if $M = 0$ and $N \neq 0$. Setting $2a - 12 = 0$ gives $a = 6$, for which the right-hand side is $12 - 3(6) = -6 \neq 0$. Thus $a = 6$.

questions.q: A delivery drone flies from depot $A$ to warehouse $B$ against a steady headwind at $36\,\mathrm{km/h}$ and returns along the same route with a tailwind at $54\,\mathrm{km/h}$. If the total round-trip flight time is $2.5$ hours, find the one-way distance $d$ between $A$ and $B$ and the average speed for the entire round trip.
questions.answer: Total time: $\dfrac{d}{36} + \dfrac{d}{54} = 2.5$. Multiply by $\mathrm{lcm}(36, 54) = 108$: $3d + 2d = 270 \Rightarrow 5d = 270 \Rightarrow d = 54\,\mathrm{km}$. Total distance is $2d = 108\,\mathrm{km}$, so average speed is $\dfrac{108}{2.5} = 43.2\,\mathrm{km/h}$ (the harmonic mean of $36$ and $54$).

questions.target: Linear Function Rate of Change & Functional Equations
questions.q: A linear function $f$ satisfies $f(2k) - f(k) = 6k$ for all real $k$, and $f(-1) = 4$. Find the formula for $f(x)$ and evaluate $f(10)$.
questions.answer: Since $f(x) = mx + b$, we have $f(2k) - f(k) = m(2k - k) = mk = 6k$, so $m = 6$. Using $f(-1) = 4$: $6(-1) + b = 4 \Rightarrow b = 10$. Therefore $f(x) = 6x + 10$ and $f(10) = 6(10) + 10 = 70$.

questions.q: A municipal water utility bills residential customers using a two-tier piecewise linear schedule: $22$ dollars base fee plus $1.80$ dollars per HCF for the first $15\,\mathrm{HCF}$, and $3.20$ dollars per HCF for every HCF above $15$. If a household's monthly bill was $81.00$ dollars, how many HCF of water did the household consume?
questions.answer: Cost at the end of Tier 1 ($15\,\mathrm{HCF}$): $22 + 1.80(15) = 22 + 27 = 49.00$ dollars. Since $81.00 > 49.00$, let $w > 15$ be total HCF: $49.00 + 3.20(w - 15) = 81.00 \Rightarrow 3.20(w - 15) = 32.00 \Rightarrow w - 15 = 10 \Rightarrow w = 25\,\mathrm{HCF}$.

sections.heading: Part I — Free-Response Questions (FRQs): Challenging & Cross-Lesson Synthesis (15–20)

questions.q: Line $\ell$ has equation $3x + 4y = 24$ and intersects the $x$-axis at $A$ and the $y$-axis at $B$. Find (a) the length of the altitude $h$ from the origin $O(0,0)$ to segment $AB$, and (b) the coordinates of the foot of the perpendicular $H$ on segment $AB$.
questions.answer: (a) The intercepts are $A(8, 0)$ and $B(0, 6)$, so $AB = \sqrt{8^2 + 6^2} = 10$. By right-triangle area, $\dfrac{1}{2}(8)(6) = \dfrac{1}{2}(10)h \Rightarrow h = \dfrac{48}{10} = 4.8$. (b) The perpendicular line through $O(0,0)$ has slope $\dfrac{4}{3}$, so $y = \dfrac{4}{3}x$. Substituting into $3x + 4y = 24$: $3x + \dfrac{16}{3}x = 24 \Rightarrow \dfrac{25}{3}x = 24 \Rightarrow x = \dfrac{72}{25} = 2.88$ and $y = \dfrac{96}{25} = 3.84$. Thus $H = (2.88, 3.84)$.

questions.q: Suppose $f(x) = ax + b$ is a linear function with $a > 0$ such that the composite function satisfies $f(f(x)) = 9x - 16$ for all real $x$. Find the exact values of $a$ and $b$, and solve $f(x) = f^{-1}(x)$.
questions.answer: Compute $f(f(x)) = a(ax + b) + b = a^2x + b(a + 1) = 9x - 16$. Since $a > 0$, $a^2 = 9 \Rightarrow a = 3$. Then $b(3 + 1) = -16 \Rightarrow 4b = -16 \Rightarrow b = -4$, so $f(x) = 3x - 4$. A fixed point satisfies $f(x) = x \Rightarrow 3x - 4 = x \Rightarrow x = 2$.

questions.q: A line with negative slope $m$ passes through the fixed point $P(3, 4)$ and forms a triangle in the first quadrant with the positive $x$- and $y$-axes. Express the x-intercept and y-intercept in terms of $m$, and verify that if $m = -\dfrac{4}{3}$, the area of the first-quadrant triangle is minimized at $A = 24$.
questions.answer: The line is $y - 4 = m(x - 3)$ with $m < 0$. Setting $y = 0$ gives the $x$-intercept $x_0 = 3 - \dfrac{4}{m}$; setting $x = 0$ gives the $y$-intercept $y_0 = 4 - 3m$. At $m = -\dfrac{4}{3}$, we obtain $x_0 = 3 - \dfrac{4}{-4/3} = 6$ and $y_0 = 4 - 3\left(-\dfrac{4}{3}\right) = 8$, giving area $A = \dfrac{1}{2}(6)(8) = 24$ (which is minimal since $A(m) = \dfrac{1}{2}\left(24 - 9m - \dfrac{16}{m}\right) \geq \dfrac{1}{2}(24 + 2\sqrt{144}) = 24$ by AM-GM).

questions.q: In a bivariate study of $n = 8$ electric vehicles, the mean battery mass is $\bar{x} = 420\,\mathrm{kg}$ and the mean driving range is $\bar{y} = 485\,\mathrm{km}$. The ordinary least-squares regression line is $\hat{y} = 0.65x + b$. (a) Use the centroid property $(\bar{x}, \bar{y})$ to find $b$. (b) If a vehicle with a $460\,\mathrm{kg}$ battery has an actual range of $501\,\mathrm{km}$, compute its residual $e = y - \hat{y}$.
questions.answer: (a) Every OLS regression line passes through $(\bar{x}, \bar{y})$: $485 = 0.65(420) + b \Rightarrow 485 = 273 + b \Rightarrow b = 212$. (b) For $x = 460$, predicted range is $\hat{y} = 0.65(460) + 212 = 299 + 212 = 511\,\mathrm{km}$. The residual is $e = y - \hat{y} = 501 - 511 = -10\,\mathrm{km}$.

questions.q: The line $y = \dfrac{3}{4}x + 5$ is tangent to a circle centered at $C(4, -2)$. Find the perpendicular distance from $C(4, -2)$ to the line, and write the standard equation of the circle.
questions.answer: Write the line in general form $3x - 4y + 20 = 0$. The perpendicular distance from $C(4, -2)$ to the tangent line equals the radius $r$: $r = \dfrac{|3(4) - 4(-2) + 20|}{\sqrt{3^2 + (-4)^2}} = \dfrac{|12 + 8 + 20|}{5} = \dfrac{40}{5} = 8$. Thus the circle has equation $(x - 4)^2 + (y + 2)^2 = 64$.

questions.q: In a laboratory calibration, temperature $C$ (in degrees Celsius) and resistance $R$ (in ohms) are linearly related. At $C = 20$, $R = 108.0\,\Omega$; at $C = 95$, $R = 138.0\,\Omega$. Meanwhile, a second sensor has resistance $R_2(C) = 96.0 + 0.65C$. At what temperature $C$ do both sensors have the exact same resistance, and what is the percentage increase in the first sensor's resistance from $C = 0$ to $C = 100$?
questions.answer: First sensor slope: $m_1 = \dfrac{138.0 - 108.0}{95 - 20} = \dfrac{30}{75} = 0.40\,\Omega/^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$. Intercept: $R_1(0) = 108.0 - 0.40(20) = 100.0\,\Omega$, so $R_1(C) = 100.0 + 0.40C$. Setting $R_1(C) = R_2(C)$: $100.0 + 0.40C = 96.0 + 0.65C \Rightarrow 0.25C = 4.0 \Rightarrow C = 16^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$. From $C = 0$ ($R_1 = 100\,\Omega$) to $C = 100$ ($R_1 = 140\,\Omega$), the percentage increase is $\dfrac{140 - 100}{100} \times 100\% = 40\%$.

sections.heading: Part II — Multiple-Choice Questions (MCQs): Foundational Concepts (21–28)

questions.q: If $4(2x - 3) + 5 = 3x + 18$, what is the value of $5x - 7$?
questions.answer: Expand: $8x - 12 + 5 = 3x + 18 \Rightarrow 5x - 7 = 18$. Notice the question asks directly for $5x - 7$, which equals $18$ without even needing to divide by $5$ ($x = 5$).

questions.q: Which of the following is an equation of the line in the $xy$-plane that has slope $-\dfrac{3}{5}$ and passes through $(10, -2)$?
questions.answer: Using point-slope form: $y - (-2) = -\dfrac{3}{5}(x - 10) \Rightarrow 5(y + 2) = -3x + 30 \Rightarrow 3x + 5y = 20$.

questions.q: What is the $x$-intercept of the graph of $\dfrac{x}{6} - \dfrac{y}{4} = 3$ in the $xy$-plane?
questions.answer: Set $y = 0$: $\dfrac{x}{6} = 3 \Rightarrow x = 18$, so the $x$-intercept is $(18, 0)$.

questions.q: A botanist models the height $h(t)$, in centimeters, of a bamboo shoot $t$ days after planting by $h(t) = 4.5t + 12$. Which statement best interprets the number $4.5$ in this context?
choices: The initial height of the shoot was $4.5\,\mathrm{cm}$.
The shoot grows an average of $4.5\,\mathrm{cm}$ per day.
The height increases by $12\,\mathrm{cm}$ every $4.5$ days.
questions.answer: In the linear model $h(t) = mt + b$, the slope $m = 4.5$ represents the constant rate of change of height with respect to time: $4.5\,\mathrm{cm}$ per day.

questions.q: Line $p$ is defined by $2y - 6x = 9$. Line $q$ is perpendicular to line $p$ in the $xy$-plane. What is the slope of line $q$?
questions.answer: Rewrite line $p$ as $y = 3x + \dfrac{9}{2}$, which has slope $m_p = 3$. A perpendicular line has negative reciprocal slope $m_q = -\dfrac{1}{3}$.

questions.q: The kinetic energy relation with linear drag work is $E = E_0 - f d$, where $E_0$ is initial energy, $f$ is friction force, and $d$ is distance. Which equation correctly expresses $d$ in terms of $E, E_0,$ and $f$?
questions.answer: Add $fd$ and subtract $E$: $fd = E_0 - E \Rightarrow d = \dfrac{E_0 - E}{f}$.

questions.q: If $\dfrac{2x + 5}{3} - \dfrac{x - 1}{2} = 4$, what is the value of $x$?
questions.answer: Multiply both sides by $6$: $2(2x + 5) - 3(x - 1) = 24 \Rightarrow 4x + 10 - 3x + 3 = 24 \Rightarrow x + 13 = 24 \Rightarrow x = 11$.

questions.q: The graph of a linear function $f$ is shown below. What is the value of $f(8)$?
questions.answer: From the plotted graph, the line passes through $(0, 3)$ and $(4, -1)$, so its slope is $m = \dfrac{-1 - 3}{4 - 0} = -1$ and $f(x) = -x + 3$. Therefore $f(8) = -8 + 3 = -5$.

sections.heading: Part II — Multiple-Choice Questions (MCQs): Intermediate Exam Practice (29–37)

questions.q: In the equation $k(3x - 4) = 6(2x - 5) + 2$, $k$ is a constant. If the equation has no solution, what is the value of $k$?
questions.answer: Expand: $3kx - 4k = 12x - 28$. For no solution, the $x$-coefficients must be equal ($3k = 12 \Rightarrow k = 4$) while the constant terms differ ($-4(4) = -16 \neq -28$). Thus $k = 4$.

questions.q: A catering company charges $450$ dollars for up to $20$ guests, plus $18.50$ dollars for each guest beyond $20$. If a client's total bill before tax was $968$ dollars, how many guests attended the event?
questions.answer: Let $g > 20$ be the total number of guests: $450 + 18.50(g - 20) = 968 \Rightarrow 18.50(g - 20) = 518 \Rightarrow g - 20 = 28 \Rightarrow g = 48$ guests.

questions.q: If $f$ is a linear function such that $f(-2) = 11$ and $f(6) = -5$, what is the $x$-intercept of the graph of $y = f(x)$?
How many real solutions does the equation $|4x - 9| + 6 = 2$ have?
questions.answer: Subtract $6$ from both sides: $|4x - 9| = -4$. Because the absolute value of any real expression is non-negative, there are zero real solutions.

questions.target: Sum of Solutions of Absolute Value Equations
questions.q: What is the sum of all solutions to the equation $2|3x - 6| = 18$?
questions.answer: Divide by $2$: $|3x - 6| = 9 \Rightarrow 3x - 6 = 9$ ($x = 5$) or $3x - 6 = -9$ ($x = -1$). The sum of the solutions is $5 + (-1) = 4$.

questions.q: Line $L$ passes through $(k, 3)$ and $(9, 2k - 1)$ in the $xy$-plane and has slope $\dfrac{3}{2}$. What is the value of $k$?
questions.answer: Use the slope formula: $\dfrac{(2k - 1) - 3}{9 - k} = \dfrac{3}{2} \Rightarrow 2(2k - 4) = 3(9 - k) \Rightarrow 4k - 8 = 27 - 3k \Rightarrow 7k = 35 \Rightarrow k = 5$.

questions.q: The line $\dfrac{x}{a} + \dfrac{y}{b} = 1$ passes through $(3, 4)$ and has slope $-\dfrac{2}{3}$. What is the value of $a + b$?
questions.answer: The slope of $\dfrac{x}{a} + \dfrac{y}{b} = 1$ is $-\dfrac{b}{a} = -\dfrac{2}{3}$, so $b = \dfrac{2}{3}a$. Substituting $(3, 4)$: $\dfrac{3}{a} + \dfrac{4}{(2/3)a} = 1 \Rightarrow \dfrac{3}{a} + \dfrac{6}{a} = 1 \Rightarrow a = 9$, and $b = \dfrac{2}{3}(9) = 6$. Thus $a + b = 9 + 6 = 15$.

questions.q: When the graph of $y = 4x - 7$ is translated $3$ units to the left and $5$ units upward in the $xy$-plane, what is the $y$-intercept of the resulting line?
questions.answer: Translating $3$ units left replaces $x$ with $x + 3$, and $5$ units upward adds $5$: $y = 4(x + 3) - 7 + 5 = 4x + 12 - 2 = 4x + 10$. The new $y$-intercept is $(0, 10)$.

questions.q: A store discounts a jacket by $20\%$ off its original price $p$, and a customer then applies a $15$-dollar coupon before paying $8\%$ sales tax on the reduced amount. If the final total is $108.00$ dollars, what was the original price $p$?
questions.answer: Set up the linear equation: $1.08(0.80p - 15) = 108.00 \Rightarrow 0.80p - 15 = 100.00 \Rightarrow 0.80p = 115.00 \Rightarrow p = 143.75$ dollars.

sections.heading: Part II — Multiple-Choice Questions (MCQs): Challenging & Cross-Lesson Synthesis (38–45)

questions.q: What is the area of the triangle enclosed by the lines $y = 2x + 4$, $y = -x + 7$, and the $x$-axis?
questions.answer: Find the vertices: $y = 2x + 4$ meets the $x$-axis at $(-2, 0)$; $y = -x + 7$ meets the $x$-axis at $(7, 0)$. The two lines intersect where $2x + 4 = -x + 7 \Rightarrow 3x = 3 \Rightarrow x = 1, y = 6$. The base along the $x$-axis is $7 - (-2) = 9$ and the altitude is $y = 6$, so Area $= \dfrac{1}{2}(9)(6) = 27$.

questions.q: In the $xy$-plane, the perpendicular bisector of the segment joining $A(-2, 1)$ and $B(6, 5)$ intersects the $y$-axis at $(0, b)$. What is the value of $b$?
questions.answer: The midpoint of $AB$ is $M = \left(\dfrac{-2+6}{2}, \dfrac{1+5}{2}\right) = (2, 3)$. The slope of $AB$ is $m_{AB} = \dfrac{5 - 1}{6 - (-2)} = \dfrac{1}{2}$, so the perpendicular bisector has slope $m_{\perp} = -2$ and equation $y - 3 = -2(x - 2) \Rightarrow y = -2x + 7$. Thus $b = 7$.

questions.q: For all real numbers $x$, the linear function $g$ satisfies $2g(x) + g(4 - x) = 6x - 3$. What is the value of $g(5)$?
questions.answer: Substitute $x = 5$: $2g(5) + g(-1) = 27$. Substitute $x = -1$: $2g(-1) + g(5) = -9$. Multiply the first equation by $2$ and subtract the second: $3g(5) = 54 - (-9) = 63 \Rightarrow g(5) = 21$.

questions.q: The line $y = mx + 5$ intersects the parabola $y = x^2 + 2x + 9$ at exactly one point in the $xy$-plane. If $m > 0$, what is the value of $m$?
questions.answer: Set $x^2 + 2x + 9 = mx + 5 \Rightarrow x^2 + (2 - m)x + 4 = 0$. For tangency (one intersection), the discriminant must be zero: $\Delta = (2 - m)^2 - 4(1)(4) = 0 \Rightarrow 2 - m = \pm 4$. Since $m > 0$, $2 - m = -4 \Rightarrow m = 6$.

questions.q: If the solution set to the inequality $|3x - a| \leq b$ is the closed interval $[-2, 6]$, what is the value of $a + b$?
questions.answer: The interval $[-2, 6]$ has midpoint $c = \dfrac{-2 + 6}{2} = 2$ and half-width $r = \dfrac{6 - (-2)}{2} = 4$. Rewriting $|3x - a| \leq b$ as $\left|x - \dfrac{a}{3}\right| \leq \dfrac{b}{3}$ gives $\dfrac{a}{3} = 2 \Rightarrow a = 6$ and $\dfrac{b}{3} = 4 \Rightarrow b = 12$. Thus $a + b = 18$.

questions.target: Linear Drainage Rate in a 3D Cylinder
questions.q: A cylindrical water tank of radius $r = 2\,\mathrm{m}$ and height $H = 10\,\mathrm{m}$ is initially full and drains at a constant volumetric rate so that the water depth $h(t)$ decreases linearly by $0.4\,\mathrm{m}$ per minute. After how many minutes does the tank contain $24\pi\,\mathrm{m^3}$ of water?
questions.answer: The volume of water at depth $h$ is $V = \pi r^2 h = 4\pi h$. When $V = 24\pi$, the depth is $h = \dfrac{24\pi}{4\pi} = 6\,\mathrm{m}$. Since $h(t) = 10 - 0.4t$, solving $10 - 0.4t = 6$ yields $0.4t = 4 \Rightarrow t = 10$ minutes.

questions.target: Coordinate Reflection Across an Oblique Line
questions.q: The reflection of the point $P(1, 7)$ across the line $y = x + 2$ has coordinates $(x_0, y_0)$. What is the value of $x_0 + y_0$?
questions.answer: The reflection of $(x_1, y_1)$ across $y = x + 2$ (or $x - y = -2$) is $(y_1 - 2, x_1 + 2) = (7 - 2, 1 + 2) = (5, 3)$. Check: midpoint is $(3, 5)$, which satisfies $5 = 3 + 2$, and slope is $\dfrac{3 - 7}{5 - 1} = -1 \perp 1$. Thus $x_0 + y_0 = 5 + 3 = 8$.

questions.target: Effect of Linear Transformations on Spread
questions.q: In a data set of $20$ observations $(x_i, y_i)$, every point lies on the line $y = -2.5x + 14$. If the standard deviation of the $x$-values is $s_x = 3.2$, what is the standard deviation $s_y$ of the $y$-values?
questions.answer: Under a linear transformation $y = mx + b$, the standard deviation scales by $|m|$ and is unaffected by the vertical shift $b$: $s_y = |-2.5| s_x = 2.5(3.2) = 8.0$.
